input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers the keyboard accessibility fixes identified by the
accessibility audit for the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. After this
epic, each of the four flows can be completed end-to-end with keyboard alone,
with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus
indicators. This is the code-remediation deliverable of the strategy; the
updated published conformance documentation is tracked separately.

## Scope

- Remediate every keyboard-operability defect enumerated in the accessibility
  audit for the four audited flows, including:
  - Focus loss in modals (focus must be moved into, contained within, and
    returned from modal dialogs correctly).
  - Controls that are unreachable via keyboard (all interactive controls in
    the audited flows must be operable without a pointer).
  - Focus traps where focus becomes stuck in a container and cannot escape.
- Make focus indicators consistent and clearly visible across all interactive
  controls in the audited flows, in line with the audit's findings on
  inconsistent indicators.
- Verify that remediation does not regress existing keyboard behavior in the
  four flows.
- Out of scope per the strategy: screen-reader semantics beyond what the
  keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using
  keyboard input alone.
- Every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit for these flows is
  resolved, or explicitly documented as waived with a stated reason.
- No focus traps remain: focus can always be moved into, within, and out of
  every modal and container in the audited flows, and focus is restored
  sensibly when a modal closes.
- No interactive control in the audited flows is unreachable or inoperable
  via keyboard.
- Focus indicators are visible and consistent across all interactive controls
  in the audited flows.
- Existing keyboard interactions in the four flows continue to work (no
  regressions introduced by the remediation).

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | Full — the four audited core flows fully operable by keyboard, no focus traps, no unreachable controls |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Full — visible focus indicators consistent across the audited flows. Bundled with HLR-1: both requirements are remediated by the same pass over the same surfaces (modals, focus management, interactive controls) in the same four flows; splitting them would double-touch every remediation site |

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic delivers the published accessibility conformance documentation
required by the strategy: the VPAT (conformance statement) and the product
documentation's accessibility statement, updated to reflect the fixed state of
the four core Dashboard flows and republished. Two public-sector customers
require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the
republished documentation is a first-class deliverable of this strategy, not
an incidental follow-up. This epic starts after the keyboard accessibility
remediation of the Dashboard flows is complete, because the conformance
statement must describe the fixed state.

## Scope

Content outline (inside the Red Hat docs content process):

- Update the VPAT to reflect the post-remediation keyboard accessibility state
  of the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the
  fixed state and republish it.
- Align the conformance claims in both documents with what the remediation
  actually delivered, including any explicitly waived defects and any
  remaining out-of-scope limitations (screen-reader semantics beyond the
  keyboard fixes, flows outside the four audited ones).
- Obtain technical review of the updated content against the implemented
  fixes before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to accurately reflect the keyboard accessibility state
  of the four audited flows after remediation.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated and
  republished.
- Every conformance claim in the updated documents is accurate against the
  implemented state, and remaining limitations are stated.
- The updated content is technically reviewed against the implementation by
  the Dashboard engineering team, and review feedback is addressed before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-3 | P2 | Full — accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review |

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

## Triage

Not below-threshold and not docs-only. Although the code scope is a single
component (Dashboard) owned by a single team with an audit enumerating the
defects, the strategy spans two architecturally distinct work streams that
warrant separate PR review cycles: Dashboard code remediation (HLR-1, HLR-2)
and substantive accessibility conformance content authoring — the VPAT and the
product docs accessibility statement, updated and republished (HLR-3). The
published conformance statement is an explicit deliverable tied to customer
renewal, not an incidental doc touch-up. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001: Dashboard keyboard accessibility remediation]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002: VPAT and accessibility statement republish]
    E001 --> E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The VPAT and accessibility statement must describe the fixed state, so the docs-authoring epic is blocked by the Dashboard remediation epic. |

No other edges: single implementation epic for the code work (same component,
same team, same logical change — audit-driven keyboard/focus remediation), and
no Investigation epics (the strategy's open questions table is explicitly
"None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow", so there are
no unknowns whose resolution would change which epics exist or what they do).

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic | Coverage |
|-----|----------|------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Full — keyboard operability, no focus traps, no unreachable controls across the four audited flows |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Full — consistent visible focus indicators across the audited flows. Bundled with HLR-1: both HLRs edit the same surfaces (modals, focus management, interactive controls) in the same four flows for the same component and team; splitting would double-touch every remediation site |
| HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Full — VPAT and product docs accessibility statement updated, republished, technically reviewed |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping

- **Dashboard** → canonical component `Dashboard` (verbatim from
  `.context/rhai-components.txt`). Active component: code changes to the four
  audited flows. Owning team per `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`:
  RHOAI Dashboard.
- **Documentation** → canonical component `Documentation` (verbatim from
  `.context/rhai-components.txt`). Content authoring work stream: VPAT update
  and accessibility statement republish, routed as `docs-authoring`.

## Priority Derivation

- E001: P1 — inherits the P1 priority of HLR-1 and HLR-2, the highest-priority
  HLRs it covers.
- E002: P2 — `docs-authoring` priority exception: strategy frontmatter
  `priority: Normal` maps to P2. Per the exception, this epic does not push its
  priority upstream to E001.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. The decomposition proceeds from the
  HLR table, Affected Components list, and problem statement. Team assignment
  for the documentation epic is an assumption: with no Impacted Teams table,
  the docs-authoring epic is assigned to RHOAI Dashboard (the team that owns
  the fixes and must provide the technical review); reassign if a dedicated
  documentation team owns the accessibility statement.
- **Epic size overage kept deliberately**: E001 covers keyboard/focus
  remediation across all four audited flows in one epic. It is kept as one
  epic because it is one logical change (audit-enumerated keyboard and focus
  defect remediation of the same kind on the same console) for one component
  and team; a split would fragment a single mechanical pass over shared focus
  management surfaces. **Re-split trigger**: re-split along flow boundaries
  (one epic per audited flow, or code-flow fixes vs. shared focus-indicator
  work) if the audit's enumerated defect list is materially larger than the
  estimate or if any single flow's remediation exceeds roughly one week of
  effort, so that review cycles can proceed in parallel.
- **Passive validation note**: no passive components — both affected
  components have deliverables in this strategy.
- **External commitment risk (not a DAG dependency)**: the published VPAT is
  required by two public-sector customers before renewal. The renewal deadline
  is a business constraint on scheduling, not an epic dependency; it is
  recorded here for planning awareness.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing. Both epics are
internally scheduled; the documentation epic simply follows the code work.
